fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. They cry out, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!" (Matthew 9:27). They don't start with a list of what they want. Mercy is the whole request in that verse.

Right, baker. Jesus goes into the house, and the text says "…the blind men came to Him." (Matthew 9:28). They had been following Him and crying out, and now they come to Him inside. Stayed outside? Not these two.

I can see why you'd say it, baker. Those two followed Jesus and kept shouting, and I bet that took real work. But the word Jesus uses is faith: "According to your faith will it be done to you." (Matthew 9:29).

Not this time, baker. Faith and family both start with F, so I get the mix-up. But no relatives show up in this scene. Jesus touches their eyes and says, "According to your faith will it be done to you." (Matthew 9:29).
Good thinking, baker, but that line isn't in this scene. Here Jesus warns them sternly, "See that no one finds out about this!" (Matthew 9:30). There's no mention of a priest in these verses.
Nice try, baker. It sounds like something Jesus would say, but it isn't in this scene. Here He says, "See that no one finds out about this!" (Matthew 9:30). That's a stern warning to keep quiet.
Yes, baker. "…when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak." (Matthew 9:33). Before that, he was mute (Matthew 9:32). Now he's talking, and that's the big change.

Not quite, baker, and I know a plain True can feel like a trick. The text says, "…when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak." (Matthew 9:33). He was mute before (Matthew 9:32), and now he talks. So the answer is True.

That's the word, baker. The text says, "The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”" (Matthew 9:33). They had just watched a man who couldn't speak start talking. Amazed is exactly what the verse says.

Not the crowds, baker. The text says they "…were amazed…" (Matthew 9:33). They also say, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!" (Matthew 9:33). Amazed is the word, and it's the one to remember.

Yes, baker. The Pharisees say, "It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons." (Matthew 9:34). The crowds had just said, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!" (Matthew 9:33). Then the Pharisees give a very different answer.

Interesting pick, baker, but Egypt never comes up in this passage. Here the Pharisees say, "It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons." (Matthew 9:34). Magic isn't in their words at all.
